name: User-Agent string
plain: The browser's self-description sent on every request and readable in JavaScript.
meaning: Tells the site browser brand and major version, OS family, and CPU family. Used for compatibility and bot filtering. Since UA reduction the string is coarse, so finer detail moved to opt-in Client Hints.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

story.what_it_is: The browser's own description of itself, sent on every request and readable by scripts.

marketing.name: User-Agent header
marketing.pitch: Docs explain the header and note that browsers now send less detail for privacy.

story.for_you: You never see it. It rides along every time you open a page. It lets the site pick the right version, like a phone layout or a desktop layout, and sort out bots.
story.for_makers: Compatibility, bot filtering and basic analytics all start here. With reduction, the string is coarse, so more people look the same. Makers often combine it with other signals to check whether a visitor is who they claim to be.

use_cases.example: A web app shows a banner for a browser version that is too old to run it.
A web firewall blocks traffic from strings known to belong to scrapers.
An ad server filters out crawlers by their strings so advertisers are not charged for them.
A product team reads strings to decide which browsers still deserve support.
A browser game shows a message to people on a browser with no WebGL.
A video player picks the right format for Safari versus Chrome.
An IT team blocks company logins from unapproved browsers.

technical_bounds: Cannot reliably state exact OS minor version on Chromium, Safari or Firefox
Can be spoofed trivially by extensions or DevTools

abuse: Combined with other signals for tracking

linkedin.how: Collected as userAgent, appName, appCodeName, appVersion, product, productSub, vendor. Read by the LinkedIn APFC fingerprint script (48 features, alleged by BrowserGate, partly confirmed by BleepingComputer).

history.change: Minor, build and patch version zeroed in UA string (101.0.0.0)
Desktop OS and CPU frozen to Windows NT 10.0, Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7, Linux x86_64
Android version frozen to 10 and device model replaced by K; phase complete by Chrome 113
macOS token already frozen at 10_15_7 (Big Sur and later still report it)
